_comment: German counterpart of blocklist.json. Same rules: exact match only, and
the same deliberate refusal to strip clinical or protective vocabulary.
Matching is lowercased, so entries are written lowercase even where German
would capitalise the noun.
German needs judgement English and Spanish did not:
1. `behindert` STAYS, and this is the most important line in the file.
It is both the ordinary word for disabled and a playground insult.
An AAC user has to be able to say `ich bin behindert` — taking that
word away to avoid the insult would silence the very people this app
exists for. The disability slurs proper (`spasti`, `mongo`,
`krüppel`) are blocked instead, which is the distinction that
matters.
2. `jude` stays. It is the ordinary word for a Jewish person; blocking
it would be its own kind of erasure. Slurs are listed by their own
form.
3. `mist`, `verflixt` and `quatsch` stay — they are what a parent says
in front of a child, and a board that cannot be mildly annoyed is
not giving anyone a full voice.
4. `schwul` stays: it is the ordinary word for gay and is used as a
self-description. `schwuchtel` is the slur and is blocked.

_why: AAC users experience abuse at far higher rates than the general
population, and lacking the vocabulary to describe bodies, sex, and
assault is a documented barrier to disclosure. Stripping clinical and
protective vocabulary out of prediction would make the app worse at the
moment it matters most. These words stay, and build-lexicon.mjs asserts
that no future blocklist edit removes them.
